reference.method: Every one of the 248 reference values is re-derived in this generator from the physics the tool declares and from the primary sources cited below -- closed-form Sabine/Eyring/mean-free-path/image-source statistics, an independently coded yaw-pitch-roll segment/plane and segment/OBB intersection, and an independently coded explicit finite-volume integration of the diffusion PDE with the Jing-Xiang modified Robin boundary factor. No stored tool output is used as a reference.
reference.input_provenance: The scene inputs (the embedded starter material library, the octave-band air attenuation table, room geometry, source/receiver placement, insertion-loss vectors) are inputs to the physics, not reference outputs. The material and air tables are the tool's own declared defaults, transcribed into this generator so it runs without the tool; every other scene number is chosen by the generator and stated in full in each case's `inputs`.

provenance_note: 247 of the 248 reference values are numbers recomputed in this generator from the declared physics and the cited sources; the remaining 1 is the model-invariance row, whose reference is not a recomputed number but the assertion that the first calculation after a rejected push equals the tool's own output for the corrected position. No case reuses a stored tool output or a frozen recorded value, so no case carries ref_source "recorded".
reference_citations: W. C. Sabine, Collected Papers on Acoustics, Harvard University Press, 1922 -- T60 = 0.161 V / A.
C. F. Eyring, "Reverberation time in dead rooms", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 1(2), 1930, pp. 217-241 -- T60 = 0.161 V / (-S ln(1-alpha_bar)).
ISO 3382-2:2008, Acoustics -- Measurement of room acoustic parameters, Part 2: Reverberation time in ordinary rooms (Sabine/Eyring statistical basis and the 4V/S mean free path).
V. Valeau, J. Picaut, M. Hodgson, "On the use of a diffusion model for acoustically coupled rooms", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 119(3), 2006, pp. 1504-1513 -- D = c*lambda/3 with lambda = 4V/S.

Y. Jing, N. Xiang, "On boundary conditions for the diffusion equation in room-acoustic prediction", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 121(6), 2007, pp. 3226-3231 -- modified Robin exchange coefficient A_M = alpha / [2(2-alpha)] (eq. 12).
J. B. Allen, D. A. Berkley, "Image method for efficiently simulating small-room acoustics", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 65(4), 1979, pp. 943-950 -- unfolded image lattice and reflection order.

I-Simpa diffusion-model validation, long room 32 x 4 x 4 m, alpha = 0.1, fully diffuse reflection, source (2,2,2), receivers on the axis at y = 5..30 m: https://i-simpa.univ-gustave-eiffel.fr/validation/validation-of-the-diffusion-model/long-room -- published QUALITATIVE behaviour (the level falls monotonically along the room); it publishes no digit-level table, so it grades the trend, not the values.

tolerance.tight: abs <= max(1e-10, 2e-9*max(1,|reference|)) -- closed form the tool claims to implement exactly, so double-precision agreement is the criterion
tolerance.loss: abs <= 1e-8 dB -- path loss is a sum of user-entered octave-band constants over the intersected objects; only the intersection test and the sum are under test
tolerance.diff: rel <= 3e-5 (floor 1e-11) -- same explicit finite-volume discretisation, but the tool stores its energy-density history in Float32 and its link-transmission coefficients in Float32, so the two integrations separate at about 1e-8 relative

strict_relative_grading.note: relative error of every numeric check, independent of the declared floors

independent_physics.what: Graded against closed forms taken from their primary statements and implemented in the generator: Sabine and Eyring reverberation, the 4V/S mean free path, area-weighted octave-band absorption and scattering including the two-sided free baffle and the near-anechoic wall opening, the unfolded image-source count through order 3, the diffusion coefficient D = c(4V/S)/3, and segment/plane plus segment/OBB intersection under a yaw-pitch-roll basis. Nothing about the tool's implementation is assumed.

implementation_faithfulness.what: The diffusion cases. The PDE, its boundary factor A_M = alpha/[2(2-alpha)] and D are independent physics, but the grid-sizing rule, the 0.40 stability factor, the 2 ms sample step, the t_end rule, the source-cell placement and the nearest-cell readout are the tool's own scheme, re-implemented in the generator from its declared description. These checks prove the tool integrates the scheme it declares; they do NOT prove the scheme is the right discretisation of the physics. They are self-checks and are not counted as independent evidence.

model_invariance.what: The tool compared with itself across two pushes of the same scene, one of them outside the declared interior placement constraint. There is no external reference for this check and it is not counted as independent evidence; it exists to pin the contract that the scene the tool reports is the scene it computed from, so the placement defect cannot come back unnoticed. The seventeen closed-form quantities graded beside it in the same scenario ARE independent.

published_qualitative.what: The I-Simpa long-room configuration publishes no digit-level table, only the behaviour that the level falls monotonically along the room. That trend is graded; the six receiver energies beside it are graded against this generator's own re-derivation, not against any published number.

not_covered: No measured validation. The PTB/Bork round-robin the manifest names as pending is still pending; nothing here compares the tool to a measured room.
The absolute calibration of the late field is normalised to the hybrid room-term budget; the diffusion solve sets the distribution, and no check here validates the absolute level.
The RIR/EDC synthesis, the auralization and the WAV export are stochastic and ungraded.
Polygon (non-shoebox) geometry, the SPL/metric map ensemble, local treatment reflection coefficients and the measurement-reference import are not exercised by these 18 scenarios.
Receiver SPL, C50/C80/D50/Ts/EDT/T20/T30 and the air-absorption table itself are not graded here.

solver_provenance.note: which backend the page reported while the diffusion cases were solved. "workers:N" = solved off the main thread through the compute runtime; "cpu" = the runtime was unreachable and the PDE was solved synchronously on the main thread.

sabine_constant.note: the tool declares and uses the textbook constant 0.161; the exact Sabine constant is 24 ln(10)/c(T). Both are computed here; the tool is graded against the form it declares, and the deviation below is the size of that modelling choice.

diffusion_storage_precision.note: the tool stores its energy-density history AND its link-transmission coefficients in Float32. Re-running the same finite-volume integration here in plain Float64, and again with both of those stores narrowed to Float32, shows which of the two the tool reproduces. Agreement with the Float32 variant at round-off, against a ~1e-8 separation from the Float64 variant, means the whole residual on the diffusion cases is the tool's storage choice and not a disagreement about the physics. The GRADED reference is the Float64 one, so the tool is never graded against an emulation of its own arithmetic.

recommended_status.evidence: 248/248 checks pass on the shipping build. 217 are independent physics and are what the tier rests on; 29 are labelled self-checks of the tool's own declared diffusion scheme, 1 grades a published qualitative trend and 1 is a model-invariance check -- those 31 are disclosed beside the independent cases and do not count towards the tier. Worst relative error 2.156e-08.
recommended_status.justification: DISCLOSED, NOT COUNTED: 29 of the 248 checks have no reference independent of the tool's own code: they re-implement the tool's declared diffusion discretisation (grid-sizing rule, 0.40 stability factor, 2 ms sample step, t_end rule, source-cell placement, nearest-cell readout) and therefore prove only that the tool integrates its own scheme correctly. They are labelled on every check and are not counted towards the tier. DISCLOSED, NOT COUNTED: 1 check grades a published qualitative trend rather than a value, because the published source carries no digit-level table. DISCLOSED, NOT COUNTED: 1 check compares the tool with itself across two pushes of the same scene, to pin the interior placement contract against regression. No measured validation exists; the PTB/Bork round-robin the manifest names as pending is still pending, and the absolute late-field calibration is unvalidated.
